_comment: Shared cross-language georeferencing vectors. Consumed by
rust/core/tests/georef_parity.rs (ifc_lite_core::GeoRefExtractor) and
packages/parser/src/georef.parity.test.ts (extractGeoreferencing).
Every `expect` block is derived from the EXPRESS schema and IFC semantics,
NOT from either implementation's current output. A test that compared the
two halves only to EACH OTHER would go green on behaviour that is wrong
the same way on both sides.
IfcMapConversion (IFC4 Add2 / IFC4X3): SourceCRS, TargetCRS, Eastings,
Northings, OrthogonalHeight, XAxisAbscissa?, XAxisOrdinate?, Scale? --
'a scaling of the three axes (x,y,z) by the same Scale, followed by an
anti-clockwise rotation about the z-axis ... and then a translation in
(x,y,z) of Eastings, Northings, OrthogonalHeight'. XAxisAbscissa and
XAxisOrdinate are the components of a DIRECTION, so only their ratio is
meaningful and the pair is normalised before use as cos/sin.
IfcProjectedCRS: Name, Description?, GeodeticDatum?, VerticalDatum?,
MapProjection?, MapZone?, MapUnit? -- MapUnit is an IfcNamedUnit, i.e.
IfcSIUnit XOR IfcConversionBasedUnit, and attribute 2 is `Prefix` on the
first but `Name` on the second.
IfcSIPrefix (EXPRESS ENUMERATION) is the AUTHORITY for the prefix set:
EXA, PETA, TERA, GIGA, MEGA, KILO, HECTO, DECA, DECI, CENTI, MILLI,
MICRO, NANO, PICO, FEMTO, ATTO. A reader that knows only a subset of
these silently reports the base unit, wrong by the prefix's own factor.
mapUnitScale is null when no MapUnit is authored: per the spec the
project length unit then applies, and neither half may invent 1.0.

cases.name: map_conversion_metre_no_rotation
map_conversion_rotated_and_scaled
cases._note: XAxisAbscissa/Ordinate = cos/sin 30 deg; the one Scale (2) applies to x, y AND z.

cases.name: map_conversion_non_unit_axis_direction
cases._note: XAxisAbscissa/Ordinate is a DIRECTION: (3,4) must behave exactly as (0.6,0.8).

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_MILLI
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.MILLI = 0.001. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 0.001 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_CENTI
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.CENTI = 0.01. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 0.01 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_DECI
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.DECI = 0.1. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 0.1 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_DECA
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.DECA = 10. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 10 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_HECTO
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.HECTO = 100. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 100 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_KILO
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.KILO = 1000. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 1000 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_MICRO
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.MICRO = 1e-06. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 1e-06 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_NANO
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.NANO = 1e-09. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 1e-09 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_MEGA
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.MEGA = 1e+06. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 1e+06 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_si_prefix_GIGA
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.GIGA = 1e+09. A reader that omits it reports METRE and is 1e+09 x wrong.

cases.name: projected_crs_unprefixed_metre
cases._note: MapUnit authored with no prefix: base METRE, scale 1.

cases.name: projected_crs_conversion_based_FOOT
cases._note: IfcConversionBasedUnit: attribute 2 is Name, not Prefix.

cases.name: projected_crs_conversion_based_INCH
cases._note: IfcConversionBasedUnit: attribute 2 is Name, not Prefix.

cases.name: projected_crs_no_map_unit_defers_to_project_unit
cases._note: MapUnit absent ($): per the spec the project length unit applies; neither half may invent a unit or a scale of 1.

cases.name: epset_map_conversion_ifc2x3
cases._note: IFC2x3 has no IfcMapConversion; the buildingSMART convention uses an ePSet_MapConversion property set.

cases.name: epset_map_conversion_millimetre_unit
cases._note: ePSet_ProjectedCRS.MapUnit is a free-text label, resolved by name.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_DECAMETRE
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.DECA = 1e1. A substring test for METRE is satisfied by DECAMETRE and answers 1.0 -- a silent 10x error. Exact match required.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_HECTOMETRE
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.HECTO = 1e2. Same substring trap as DECAMETRE, 100x.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_KILOMETRE
cases._note: One of the prefixed spellings a METRE substring test collapses onto 1.0.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_MICROMETRE
cases._note: IfcSIPrefix.MICRO = 1e-6.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_METER_US_SPELLING
cases._note: The METER spelling is the unprefixed base unit, scale 1.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_FOOT
cases._note: Conversion-based length unit, from the same table the native IfcConversionBasedUnit path uses.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_US_SURVEY_FOOT
cases._note: The US survey foot is a different ratio from the international foot; separators are folded away before the exact match.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_SQUARE_METRE_REFUSED
cases._note: An area unit is not a length unit. A METRE substring test answered 1.0 here. No exact answer exists, so the reader must decline and let the project length unit apply -- an absent value is honest, a wrong one relocates the model.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_UNKNOWN_REFUSED
cases._note: BANANA is not an IfcSIPrefix member. Stripping the METRE spelling must not fall through to the base unit: refuse rather than approximate.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_METRES_PLURAL
cases._note: MapUnit is exporter free text and the plural is an ordinary real spelling. An exact-match table keyed on the EXPRESS singular refuses it unless one plural suffix is stripped first.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_METERS_PLURAL
cases._note: The US spelling, pluralised. METER and METRE are the same unit, so both must carry the plural.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_metres_lowercase
cases._note: Case-folded AND singularised: exporters write free text, not the EXPRESS enumeration casing.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_Meters_MIXED_CASE
cases._note: Mixed case plus plural, the shape a GIS exporter writes.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_MILLIMETRES_PLURAL
cases._note: A prefixed spelling, pluralised: must resolve to the MILLI factor, never to 1.0 and never be refused.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_MILLIMETERS_PLURAL
cases._note: US spelling of the same, pluralised.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_KILOMETERS_PLURAL
cases._note: Plural, US spelling and an SI prefix at once.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_DECAMETRES_PLURAL
cases._note: The regression guard for the plural rule itself: stripping the plural must land on DECAMETRE (10), NOT collapse the prefixed spelling onto the bare metre (1.0) the way the substring test did.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_INCHES_PLURAL
cases._note: An -ES plural whose singular is not reachable by dropping a single S.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_US_SURVEY_FOOT_PARENTHESISED
cases._note: US survey foot with the qualifier trailing and parenthesised. Gluing the alphanumerics gives FOOTUSSURVEY, which no glued-alias list contains: the tokens must be matched without regard to order.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_US_SURVEY_FEET_WORD_ORDER
cases._note: The same unit in a third word order, with the FEET spelling. 1200/3937, not the international 0.3048.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_SQUARE_METRES_REFUSED
cases._note: Negative control for the plural rule: stripping a plural must not turn an area unit into a length. SQUARE METRE is already pinned; its plural must decline too.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_SURVEY_FOOT_NO_NATION_REFUSED
cases._note: Negative control for the US-survey token rule: other national survey feet exist (Indian, Clarke) at different ratios, so the qualifier without US does not identify the value. Decline rather than guess.

cases.name: epset_map_unit_label_ABBREVIATION_M_REFUSED
cases._note: Negative control: a bare abbreviation is not in the derived set. m/mm/mtr are guesses, and a wrong MapUnit relocates the model.
